title: HTTP/2 compressed headers can amplify server memory usage with built-in TLS
summary: Yopass leaves MaxHeaderBytes unset on its application and metrics listeners. An unauthenticated client can repeat HPACK-compressed cookie fields across concurrent HTTP/2 requests; Go expands the headers into per-request strings retained while bodies are pending. Requires an HTTP/2-enabled built-in TLS listener or a proxy that forwards large decoded headers. Historical releases without HTTP/2 support are not exposed to this variant; this does not reveal secret content or bypass secret authorization.
ai_role: The Yopass maintainer's case-specific security advisory explicitly credits Anthropic's OSS Scanner as discoverer (tracking identifier ANT-2026-AX5EL1AH). It does not name a model version or internal discovery date.
classification_note: The public maintainer advisory documents the finding; it does not establish whether defenders knew of it or whether it was exploited before disclosure.
remediation_note: Yopass 16.0.0 fixes the issue (commit 23b56941c7597690e17907f90d4c0fe6d90049a). Affected-version scope: Built-in TLS versions 4.0.1 through 15.1.0, subject to runtime and listener configuration; fixed in 16.0.0 by setting MaxHeaderBytes to 16 KiB on both listeners. Patch availability does not establish downstream deployment.

impacts.conditions: Repeated concurrent requests can degrade availability or exhaust process/container memory under the stated HTTP/2 and listener conditions.
impacts.exploitation: The advisory describes a possible or reproducible trigger as stated; it does not report observed exploitation in the wild.
